newsitem.title: GERMANY: Havel says NATO should stick to expansion - paper.
newsitem.headline: Havel says NATO should stick to expansion - paper.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel called upon the West to stay firm on its plans for the eastward expansion of NATO despite opposition from Russia, a German newspaper reported on Friday.

The West must look for the best chances for cooperation with Russia and not treat the country as the enemy, Havel told the Saechsischen Zeitung according to a report released ahead of publication on Saturday.
The daily said Havel made the comments in an interview on Thursday, when U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin started two days of talks in Helsinki on NATO enlargement.
Havel said there could be no going back on plans for the expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and that this meant troops and weapons had to be stationed in any new member countries.
The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are the leading candidates to be invited to join NATO after an alliance summit in Madrid in July.
Russia bitterly opposes the expansion of the former Soviet Union's old Cold War foe on to territory once under the sway of the Moscow-dominated Warsaw Pact.
Havel said he would address the German parliament next month in a symbolic gesture of support for a post-World War Two reconciliation pact approved by the two countries this month.
He said German President Roman Herzog would do the same in Prague.
